questions.text: (i) Is there any displacement when no force acts on a body? Justify. (ii) Write two conditions for work to be done. (iii) Define energy. (iv) Express 1 kWh in joules.

questions.text: Which class emerged due to the Industrial Revolution?
questions.answer: The working class (labour class), along with the capitalist class.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "Management is an art of getting things done through other people." Who stated this?
questions.answer: Mary Parker Follett

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What is division of labour?
questions.answer: Dividing a job into small tasks so that each worker does one task and becomes skilled at it.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What does industrialization indicate?
questions.answer: The growth of industries, a shift from farming to manufacturing, and economic development.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Revolution and Rise of Nation States
questions.text: "Man is born free, but everywhere he is in chains." Who stated this?
questions.answer: Jean-Jacques Rousseau

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What are the qualifications required to become a Governor?
questions.answer: He or she must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, not a member of Parliament or a State Legislature, and not hold any office of profit.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What are the qualifications required to become a judge of the Supreme Court?
questions.answer: A citizen of India who has been a High Court judge for at least five years, or a High Court advocate for ten years, or a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Religion is a significant agent of socialization. How?
questions.answer: Religion teaches values such as honesty, discipline, compassion and tolerance through rituals, festivals and teachings, shaping a person's behaviour.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The rural community is significant in India. How?
questions.answer: Most Indians live in villages, agriculture is the main livelihood, and villages supply food and raw materials and preserve culture.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Briefly explain the economic system during the period of the Delhi Sultanate.
questions.answer: Agriculture was the main occupation, with land revenue as the main income. The iqta system supported administration, trade flourished with coins like the tanka and jital, and markets were regulated under Alauddin Khalji.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List the areas of our state where iron ore is found.
questions.answer: Ballari, Hosapete, Sandur, Chitradurga, Tumakuru, Chikkamagaluru (Kudremukh and Baba Budan hills) and Shivamogga.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What are the occupations in the tertiary sector?
questions.answer: Trade, transport, banking, insurance, communication, teaching, health care and other services.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What precautionary measures should you take while shopping online?
questions.answer: Use trusted websites and secure payment methods, never share OTP or card PIN, read reviews and return policy, and keep the bill and order details.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "The role of Srimanta Shankaradeva was significant in the cultural and religious history of Assam." How?
questions.answer: He spread Vaishnavism (Ekasarana dharma) through namghars and satras, and created literature, music (Borgeet) and drama (Ankiya Nat).
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Preservation of historical monuments is the responsibility of everyone. Justify.
questions.answer: Monuments show our history and culture, attract tourists and give income, and once damaged cannot be replaced, so all citizens must protect them.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What were the philosophies propounded by Shankaracharya?
questions.answer: Advaita (non-dualism): Brahman is the only reality, the world is maya, and the soul and Brahman are one; knowledge (jnana) leads to liberation.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What were the welfare measures introduced by Basavanna?
questions.answer: He set up Anubhava Mantapa, opposed caste and gender discrimination, promoted equality and dignity of labour (Kayaka), and encouraged simple Kannada vachanas.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List the major ports of Karnataka.
questions.answer: New Mangalore, Karwar, Belekeri, Malpe, Honnavar, Tadadi and Bhatkal.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List the geographical factors suitable for growing rice.
questions.answer: A hot, humid climate with 20–30 °C temperature, heavy rainfall of 150 cm or more or good irrigation, and fertile alluvial or clayey soil on flat land.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Write about the importance of banks in the economy.
questions.answer: Banks keep savings safe, give loans to farmers, traders and industries, encourage saving and investment, provide payment services and support economic growth.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Write about the importance of labour in production.
questions.answer: Labour turns raw materials into goods, uses machines, creates incomes and employment, and no production is possible without it.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List the functional areas of management.
questions.answer: Production, marketing, finance and human resources management.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List the functions of a market.
questions.answer: Bringing buyers and sellers together, exchange of goods and services, price fixing, storing and transport, and giving information about products.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: The Ahom Dynasty, The Mughals and the Marathas
questions.text: "The establishment of the Maratha kingdom opened a new chapter in Indian history." Justify.
questions.answer: Shivaji founded an independent Hindu kingdom, built a strong army, navy and forts, created an efficient administration (Ashtapradhan), and challenged the Mughals.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "In India the electoral process consists of multiple stages." Justify.
questions.answer: Stages include delimitation of constituencies, preparing voters' lists, announcing the schedule, filing nominations, campaigning, voting, counting and declaring results.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Soil erosion is reducing land fertility. As a farmer, what is your role in controlling it?
questions.answer: Practise contour ploughing and terracing, grow cover crops and rotate crops, plant trees as shelter belts, and avoid overgrazing.
questions.review: Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain the teachings of Jesus Christ.
questions.answer: Love God and your neighbour, forgive others, be humble and truthful, serve the poor, and live in peace and non-violence.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Write the characteristics of a joint family.
questions.answer: Members of several generations live together, share a common kitchen and property, are led by the eldest, and share duties and bring up children together.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Mention the effects of the Industrial Revolution.
questions.answer: Factories and machines replaced hand production, cities grew, a working class and capitalist class emerged, trade and transport expanded, but workers faced poor conditions and pollution rose.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Mention the causes of the Religious Reformation.
questions.answer: Corruption in the Church, sale of indulgences, the printing press, Renaissance ideas, and leaders such as Martin Luther challenging the Pope.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "Industries contribute significantly to a country's economic development." Analyze.
questions.answer: Industries create jobs, raise national income, use raw materials, increase exports, support agriculture and services, and raise living standards.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4. Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Localization of industries is influenced by many factors. Justify.
questions.answer: Industries settle where raw materials, power, water, labour, transport, markets, capital and government policy are available.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4. Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How can you say that the economic system of the Vijayanagara Empire was prosperous?
questions.answer: Agriculture was supported by tanks and canals, trade by land and sea was rich, and cities such as Hampi had busy markets for diamonds and spices. Industries such as textiles and mining flourished, and gold coins were used.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Mention the features of the Indian Constitution.
questions.answer: It is the longest written constitution; it provides a Preamble, fundamental rights and duties, directive principles, a parliamentary system, federalism, an independent judiciary, secularism and universal adult franchise.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4.

questions.text: On the outline map of Karnataka, mark any five of: A) Aurad B) New Mangalore C) Canara coast D) Shivanasamudra E) Tungabhadra River F) Mahatma Gandhi Hydroelectric Station G) Bhadravati H) The Manchester of Karnataka I) Silicon Valley J) Belagavi.
